lab.title: Choosing if/else, a switch Statement, or a switch Expression
lab.objective: Choose if/else, switch statements, or switch expressions based on the shape of a decision.
lab.task: Choose and handle a customer-support ticket priority.
lab.startingCondition: Prerequisites: the .NET SDK, VS Code or another C# editor, and basic ability to run dotnet commands. No numbered session or optional module is required. Create exercises/optional/support-ticket-decisions from scratch.

steps.text: Step 1/12: Create an isolated console project with dotnet new console -o exercises/optional/support-ticket-decisions. Do not add it to PinkMachine19.TimeClock.sln and do not edit TimeClock production code.
Step 2/12: Open exercises/optional/support-ticket-decisions/Program.cs and remove only the template Hello World statement.
Step 3/12: At the top of Program.cs, add a comment naming the scenario: Choose and handle a customer-support ticket priority.
Step 4/12: Create waitingHours and channel inputs for one support ticket.
Step 5/12: Use if/else for the unrelated Boolean escalation conditions.
Step 6/12: Use a switch statement for channel-specific actions that require multiple statements.
Step 7/12: Use a switch expression to produce one priority label from waiting-hour ranges.
Step 8/12: Add a default or discard path so every input has an outcome.
Step 9/12: Run three input combinations and predict which construct handles each decision.
Step 10/12: Write one comment explaining why none of the three constructs is universally best.
Step 11/12: Build with dotnet build exercises/optional/support-ticket-decisions --configuration Release. Read any diagnostic before changing code.
Step 12/12: Run with dotnet run --project exercises/optional/support-ticket-decisions --configuration Release, then open Solution Reveal and compare every line.
